title: Meta-tagging & edgecase sampler (wip)
content:
Quick notes: collecting a small, focused sampler of weird/ambiguous records for the labeler rotation. Goal: reduce manual triage time and make provenance tags reliable so downstream evals can filter by origin and precleaning applied. This is a working scratchpad — many TODOs and open q's below.

Summary of intent:
- Build a 1.5k item "edgecase sampler" dataset that covers: long URLs, embedded code, mixed-language snippets, numeric units with locale variants, nested entities, truncated sentences, punctuation noise, non-standard quotes, tokenization artifacts (-zero-width), and OCR-like garbled text.
- Each item should have a primary label + meta-tags: source_provenance, preclean_applied, tokenization_flag, ambiguity_level (low/med/high).
- Use for: spot checks, labeler training, automatic heuristic coverage tests, and as a failing set for regression alerts.

Labeling heuristics (draft):
1) Primary label precedence:
   - If span matches an explicit user-facing ID pattern (account id, order#) -> label ID.
   - If span is ambiguous between NAME and ORG choose ORG only when contextual cue tokens present (Ltd, Inc, Corp, LLC, team, org).
   - Date/Time heuristics: prefer ISO-ish or tokens with month names; numeric-only sequences >4 digits -> treat as ID unless surrounded by date tokens.

2) Overlapping spans:
   - Allow nested spans if both are naturally meaningful (e.g., "Amazon" inside "Amazon Web Services").
   - If overlap is accidental (partial token overlap due to tokenization) -> normalize to token boundaries and label the largest meaningful span.

3) Tokenization flagging:
   - Mark tokenization_flag=split-utf8 when input contains U+200B/U+FEFF or unusual combining marks.
   - For hyphenation splits: if token contains hyphenated compound that is not punctuation-only (e.g., "x-ray"), label whole compound.

Provenance tags (important):
- src:web-crawl, src:user-upload, src:ocr, src:internal-mock, src:synth-perturb
- preclean:none, preclean:strip-html, preclean:whitespace-norm, preclean:unicode-normalize
- Why: downstream evals should be able to exclude OCR or synth-perturb samples when measuring "real-world" precision.

Sampling notes (how to build the 1.5k):
- Start with stratified buckets by src: 40% web-crawl, 20% user-upload, 15% ocr, 15% synth-perturb, 10% internal-mock.
- For long-tail tokens (rare named entities), run priority sampling from ERROR logs (see DATA-1423) and dedupe by fingerprint to avoid duplicates.
- Use active learning loop: seed 300 labeled, train small classifier, sample top-uncertainty 700, label those. Remaining fill by targeted heuristics for specific edge-case types.

Example rows (format: id | src | raw_text | primary_label(s) | meta-tags)
- 0001 | src:ocr | "libr@ry ᚠ 12/??/19" | ORG(?) | [preclean:none, tokenization_flag:unicode-weird, ambiguity_level:high]
- 0022 | src:web-crawl | "https://example.com/path?utm_ref=Ðx%F3" | URL | [preclean:strip-html, tokenization_flag:percent-encoded, ambiguity_level:med]
- 0177 | src:user-upload | "Invoice #A-0041123 (due 01/02/23)" | ID, DATE | [preclean:whitespace-norm, ambiguity_level:low]
- 0310 | src:synth-perturb | "Привет, my name is Алексей-ivanovic" | PERSON | [preclean:unicode-normalize, tokenization_flag:hyphen-mixed-script, ambiguity_level:med]

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we treat email-like handles (user@example) as IDs or CONTACT? current lean: ID only if structured; otherwise CONTACT. agree/disagree? (ping @#labeling on slack)
- Should src:synth-perturb be excluded from production quality alerts or only tagged? I think excluded for precision/recall, included for robustness metrics.
- How strict to be on nested spans for product features that expect atomic slots (e.g., autofill)? we might need a secondary "flattened" label pass for feature compatibility.

Quick heuristics to implement in the labeling UI (for labeler prompts):
- Show provenance, show preclean_applied, show last-annotation timestamp from other labelers (if exists).
- Provide one-click templates: "Mark as ID", "Mark as Ambiguous -> queue for triage", "Mark tokenization issue -> add tokenization_flag".
- Warn if sample appears to be dup of an existing fingerprint (show link).

Small checklist for curating initial batch:
- [ ] Pull 500 candidate web-crawl items using heuristics (URLs, long tokens, percent-encoded chars).
- [ ] Pull top 200 OCR edgecases from TABLE-ocr-error-report.csv (see linked artifact).
- [ ] Generate 200 synth-perturb variations using random unicode injections and hyphenation scripts.
- [ ] Reserve 200 for active-learning loop.
- [ ] 1st review pass by Maya + Rina, then rotate labelers for calibration.

Notes to self (personal):
- Keep sampler small enough to run fast in the eval pipeline (< 5s per item to compute heuristics).
- Add a tiny metrics sheet later: columns -> id, src, primary_label, meta-tags, label_time_secs, labeler, notes. Maybe keep that as a separate sheet.
- Remind legal to check user-upload policy for examples with PII before we include in review batches.

References / links (quick):
- DATA-1423: labeler triage logs and sampling rationale.
- GitHub PR 87: initial schema for meta-tags (needs revision for ambiguity_level).
- Slack: #labeling thread 'provenance tags v2' (Nov 2, 2025).

End — will flesh out sampling script and produce a csv extractor next week.

TODOs for next session:
- Draft labeler UI microcopy for tokenization_flag options.
- Prototype sampler script and run dedupe + fingerprinting.
- Get 2nd opinion from SRE about fingerprint collision risk for web-crawl IDs.

Random small idea: a "fuzzy provenance" score (0-1) combining heuristics: timestamp presence, content-URL-signals, checksum entropy. Use as a filter knob in eval dashboards so PMs can dial how much "trust" to give to data origin.
